display.title: The Neshamah's Secret
display.summary_short: After a talk on the mitzvah of payos, the Baal Shem Tov comforts a grieving couple with the secret of a holy neshamah, and tells them how to earn a son: Rabbi Aharon of Karlin.
display.summary_long: The storyteller begins with a teaching of the Frierdiker Rebbe: Yidden who are careful with payos and tzitzis feel a special warmth for all of Torah. He explains the mitzvah of payos and tells how the Rebbe, at a Chassid's son's first haircut, said how long a child's payos should be. Then comes the story of how Rabbi Aharon of Karlin was born. A hidden tzaddik, Rabbi Yaakov, and his wife receive the Baal Shem Tov's blessing for a son, but the boy passes away at the age of two. The Baal Shem Tov comforts them with a secret: the story of a holy neshamah born as a king's son to save the Jews, who studied with a Pope who was secretly a Jew, later became a ger tzedek, and needed only two years with a Jewish mother to be complete. The Baal Shem Tov then tells the couple to answer Amen with small children, lift them to kiss the Sefer Torah and mezuzah, and help poor new mothers, keeping yarmulkes and negel vasser for newborn boys. Two years later their son Aharon is born. The storyteller closes with the Frierdiker Rebbe's introduction to the story and the seven lessons the Alter Rebbe drew from it.
display.lesson: Ahavas Yisroel means going out of your way to comfort another Jew; small mitzvos with young children, like answering Amen, kissing the Sefer Torah and mezuzah, and early chinuch, carry great merit.

advisories.note: A couple's two-year-old son passes away; the parents grieve.
A neshamah stands before the Heavenly court and returns in a new life (gilgul).
A king threatens to expel the Jews if he has no child.
